about.title: About us
about.lead: We build Arma Reforger mods: co-op PvE campaigns with an enemy that thinks, systems for mission makers, and configuration packs for the communities we play with. This station is the official documentation of every one of them.
about.unit_p: An independent modding studio. Our Arma Reforger mods are published on the Workshop under the author name TheUnknownTeam.
about.roster_d: Only the names published on our Workshop pages are listed here.
about.r_valaaks: CTRP team contributor: SAMU equipment in ChercheToi RP - Clothing
about.d.0: On the shoulders of giants. We build on other creators' mods as declared dependencies and credit them on every page. Nothing repacked.
about.d.1: Documented settings. Every server setting ships with its own help text, right next to it in the file.
about.d.2: Tested before release. Changes go through a real dedicated-server test bench and a review before they reach the Workshop.
about.d.3: Readable by players. The enemy cheats less and tells you more: signal lights on drones that change colour when they spot you, radio hints, sirens before a strike.
about.d.4: Respect the licences. Our mods are released under the Arma Public Licence (APL or APL-ND, as stated on each page).
about.th.0: Everon — INDFORGE - Conflict PvE, Off-Road Vehicles (Game Master)
about.c.0: [AUC] Arma Ukraine Community — AUC - Factions, AUC - Vehicles, AUC - Conflict.
about.c.1: CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE — ChercheToi RP - Clothing, Props and Vehicles.
about.c.2: Task Force Baguette — TalibanMod Red Side V2.
about.contact_p: Comment on the mod's Workshop page and include: the mod version, the map and scenario, your other active mods, what you expected, what actually happened, and the steps to reproduce it.
about.motto: Alone we go faster, but together we go further… and always beyond the possible.

admins.title: Admins
admins.lead: Install a dedicated server, load our mods, set them up from the profile files and drive them with in-game commands. Everything here is generic: no real server, address, port or password.
admins.install_s.0: Install Arma Reforger Server (Steam tool, or SteamCMD with app ID 1874900), or rent a game server from a host.
admins.install_s.1: Write a configuration file, for example server.json (structure below).
admins.install_s.2: Start the server with -config pointing to that file and -profile pointing to a folder it can write to. That folder is what our mods call $profile:.
admins.install_s.3: Add our mods to game.mods: each mod page gives the full block ready to paste, and the scenario ID to put in game.scenarioId.
admins.install_s.4: Start once, stop, then drop our config.json files into the profile folder (section 4) and start again.
admins.json_p: The usual structure of a Reforger dedicated-server configuration. Fill in your own values; ports shown are the documented defaults. Keep passwordAdmin out of any file you share.
admins.json_persist: game.gameProperties.persistence.autoSaveInterval sets the autosave interval (minutes). The persistence block belongs inside gameProperties: at the root or directly in game, the server refuses to start.
admins.scen_p: Value for game.scenarioId. The mods list comes from the mod's own page.
admins.profile_s.0: $profile: is the folder given to the server with -profile. A file named $profile:INDFORGE_Weather/config.json lives in <profile>/INDFORGE_Weather/config.json.
admins.profile_s.1: A missing file is created with its defaults at startup. An existing file is never overwritten: to take a new default, put the reference copy back.
admins.profile_s.2: Every key Name comes with a help key _Name right above it. The mod never reads help keys: they are there for you, and can be deleted.
admins.profile_s.3: Most files are read once at startup: restart the server after a change. Never edit a file while the server writes to it.
admins.profile_s.4: Do not delete a key to "go back to default": the code fallback is not always the shipped value. Copy the original value back instead.
admins.cmds_p: Typed in the in-game chat by a player with the server administrator or session administrator role, or sent through RCON with admin permission. Answers come back in the chat.
admins.cfg_p: Every key of our server files with its shipped value and its help text, read from the reference copies. Help texts are quoted in English, as in the files.
admins.logs_p: Our systems write tagged lines in the server log. Search for these tags to follow what they do:
admins.logs_s.0: INDFORGE enemy HQ: tracks, groups sent, plans, ambushes, strikes, and a summary every 5 minutes.
admins.logs_s.1: INDFORGE AI doctrine: at startup, on weather changes and every 5 minutes.
admins.logs_s.2: INDFORGE generator capture:, INDFORGE generator breach: and INDFORGE fuel truck: base capture.
admins.logs_s.3: INDFORGE hunter size:, INDFORGE drone sight:, INDFORGE patrol trucks:, INDFORGE session: — and, in the next update, INDFORGE weather:, INDFORGE night gear:, INDFORGE drone team:, INDFORGE radio alerts:.
admins.logs_s.4: AI Framework: lines starting with [INDF_CombatHeliConfig], [INDF_POIManager], [INDF_MilitaryGarrisonManager] and [INDF_CombatHeliSpawner].
cmd.setrank: Sets a player's rank. Exact in-game name, then the rank name (PRIVATE, CORPORAL, SERGEANT, LIEUTENANT, CAPTAIN, MAJOR…) or its number. The rank is saved across restarts.
cmd.aidoctrine: Shows, reloads, enables or disables the AI doctrine.
cmd.aidoctrine_mod: Multiplies every engagement range by a factor, for some seconds or until switched off, to react to an event without a restart.
cmd.enemyhq: Shows the enemy headquarters: tracks, groups, plans.
cmd.enemyhq_here: Sends a fake sighting of yourself to the enemy HQ (as a drone contact and/or a vehicle), for tests.
cmd.enemyhq_rb: Lists the persistent roadblocks, or removes them all.
cmd.enemyhq_strike: Triggers an air strike or a Geran salvo in front of the admin, for tests.
cmd.weather: Weather director: status, force the next episode, hold fog, rain or wind values, resume, switch off or on.
cmd.nightgear: Night-vision and thermal equipment of the AI: counts and settings.
intel.title: News
intel.lead: What we know of the USSR/FIA command you face in INDFORGE - Conflict PvE and INDFORGE - Forest. Read it before you deploy.
intel.summary_p: The enemy no longer knows where you are by magic. Its headquarters acts on reports: what its drones and patrols actually see. It predicts where you are going, chooses a plan, calls its mortars and adapts to weather and night. Stay unseen and it stays blind.
intel.hq_s.0: Sources. An enemy drone contact, or an enemy group that identifies a player or a player vehicle. Close reports merge into a track: last known position, time, source, on foot or in a vehicle.
intel.hq_s.1: Dispatch. A fresh track gets a group, spawned on a road far from every player. Drone intel brings special forces; a patrol report brings hunters. A spotted vehicle brings an anti-vehicle team.
intel.hq_s.2: Prediction. Two reports give your direction and speed. The group heads where you should be by now, not where you were seen.
intel.hq_s.3: Search. A cold track is searched around its estimated position, on a radius that grows with time, then the group returns.
intel.hq_s.4: Formations. Column on the march, wedge on approach, line on assault and on contact.
intel.hq_s.5: Size. Hunter groups and helicopter paratroopers grow with the number of players nearby.
intel.doctrine_p: Every enemy soldier follows a doctrine level that sets when he opens fire on infantry, from how far, and how he withdraws.
intel.lvl.boot: FIA soldiers, hunters sent on a patrol report
intel.lvl.grunt: Regular USSR and US infantry, squad marksmen
intel.lvl.operator: Spetsnaz, KLMK, recon, special forces, modern US AI
intel.lvl.overwatch: Special-forces snipers and their spotters only
intel.doctrine_s.0: Fire discipline. A group that spots you before you see it holds its fire and closes in.
intel.doctrine_s.1: Tactical withdrawal. Caught off guard, half the group falls back firing while the other half sprints to cover, then they swap, regroup and come back.
intel.doctrine_s.2: Ranges depend on your posture and movement, the weapon, the group size, night and weather. A target that fires loses the benefit of its posture.
intel.fires_s.0: Mortar batteries set up in an enemy base 900 m to 3.5 km from the target, out of towns, with a crew, sentries and a patrol.
intel.fires_s.1: An observer is required: a group leader or a recon drone must see you, and you must stay put long enough. Ranging rounds come first, then fire for effect.
intel.fires_s.2: Counter-battery play: the batteries can be found and destroyed.
intel.drones_p: Enemy drones see you by distance, posture and cover:
intel.drones_s.0: Standing still cuts these ranges by 30 %. Night and weather cut them further.
intel.drones_s.1: Any foliage between you and the drone hides you — even the bush you hide in. Under 15 m, the drone's own test applies.
intel.drones_s.2: A drone that loses you hunts where it last saw you for about two minutes.
intel.drones_s.3: Back-pack jammers stop FPV drones within 50 m.
intel.light_p: A small light under the enemy Mavic tells you what it is doing. Never on an FPV.
intel.light_rf: Fast red blink: guiding a glide bomb
intel.light_o: Orange blink: searching where it lost you
intel.plans_p: For each track, the HQ scores what it knows — on foot or in a vehicle, still or moving, grouped players, inside a base, night, fog, rain, drones available, mortars, recent losses — then picks a plan:
intel.plan.0: L-shaped attack — one group fixes you at 200 m, a second flanks at 90°, both assault together.
intel.plan.1: Hammer and anvil — one group blocks the road ahead of a moving target, the other pushes.
intel.plan.2: Mortar first — the battery strikes, the group waits out of the danger zone, then assaults.
intel.plan.3: Infiltration — special forces creep in close, at night or in fog.
intel.plan.4: Feint — one group shows itself and attacks, the second waits on another axis.
intel.plan.5: Harassment — a sniper team on high ground plus the mortar, against a strong position.
intel.plans_esc: Escalation. Every group you wipe out nearby makes the next ones bigger and sharper, and favours the mortar.
intel.ambush_s.0: The HQ follows the road ahead of your vehicle and sets a kill zone 400 to 600 m further, on the high side.
intel.ambush_s.1: Nine variants: lone AT team, L-shaped, mines and fire, the trap (road closed behind you), the bait (a wreck on the road), FPV corridor, close night ambush, long-range hunter on a crest, and a pre-registered mortar strike at a junction.
intel.ambush_s.2: Persistent roadblocks appear on the paved roads you use most, and move every couple of days.
intel.ambush_s.3: Nobody fires before you enter the zone: the first rocket, then everyone.
intel.air_s.0: Glide bomb on players on foot that a Mavic keeps in sight — its red light blinks fast. Shoot the drone or break its view.
intel.air_s.1: Cruise missile on a base you just took from the enemy. The base siren sounds before impact.
intel.air_s.2: Su-57 reconnaissance passes can report you to the HQ.
intel.air_s.3: Geran raids from launch trucks parked on roads kilometres away. Kill the truck or its driver and the raid stops.
intel.air_s.4: Never on a faction's main base, never danger-close to enemy soldiers, never when the weather grounds aircraft.
intel.weather_s.0: Credible episodes in sequence: clear, fair, cloudy, overcast, drizzle, rain, thunderstorm fronts, dawn mist, fog banks — with smooth transitions.
intel.weather_s.1: Drones are grounded from 10 m/s of wind, heavy rain or thick fog; helicopter drops and waves from 14 m/s; paratroopers from 8 m/s.
intel.weather_s.2: Fog and rain shorten what mortar observers can see. Thermal sights see through light fog.
intel.night_s.0: Some soldiers get night-vision goggles — more often snipers and special forces, less often by day.
intel.night_s.1: What a soldier sees comes from what he carries: naked eye, night vision or thermal scope. Some enemy drones carry a thermal camera.
intel.radio_p: Short radio-style hints reach the players concerned: drone overhead, interception group on the way, mortar, Geran, missile, jet, ambush. Never the enemy's exact position.
intel.base_s.0: Standing in the zone no longer takes a generator base: repair the generator with a wrench, then fill it with 18 L of fuel while the siren sounds. Radio contact with your HQ is required.
intel.base_s.1: About 30 s after you take it, the nearest enemy soldier walks to the generator to sabotage it (8 s). Kill him first.
intel.base_s.2: Wall the generator in with HESCO and a breacher lays demolition charges on the closest wall: 20 s fuse, kill him or defuse.
intel.guide_s.0: Stay spread out: enemy rocket launchers also fire at infantry.
intel.guide_s.1: Break the line of sight with foliage, go prone, keep still under a drone.
intel.guide_s.2: Once spotted, change direction: they aim where you should be, not where you were.
intel.guide_s.3: Watch the Mavic light. Red: you are watched. Fast red blink: move, now.
intel.guide_s.4: A siren at your base means a strike is coming: get out of the base.
intel.guide_s.5: Kill the saboteur before he reaches the generator.
intel.state_note: Items marked Incoming are merged in development and arrive with the next Workshop update of Conflict PvE.

e404.title: Signal lost
e404.p: This frequency carries nothing. The address may be wrong, or the page has moved.
e404.hint: Tune in: drag, scroll or use the arrow keys. Follow the meter.
e404.msg: INDFORGE HQ to {cs}. The page “{path}” does not exist on this net.
e404.sos: Distress call received. Help is on its way: follow “Back to command”.
e404.joke.0: Reminder: a missing page is not lost, it is on an infiltration mission.
e404.joke.1: Last contact: the page followed a waypoint and never came back.
e404.joke.2: Engineers report: the bridge to this page is down. Detour above.
e404.joke.3: The FOB cook swears it was still here this morning.
e404.joke.4: Good listening, operator. SIGINT could not have done better.
e404.joke.5: Standing order: never turn the radio dial at random. Ah, too late.
m.conflict-pve.tag: Co-op PvE Conflict on Everon: US players against an enemy that thinks.
m.conflict-pve.intro.0: INDFORGE - Conflict PvE turns the Conflict mode into a cooperative PvE campaign on Everon. Players fight as the US; the USSR and the FIA are run by AI with a combat doctrine, a headquarters that acts on intelligence, mortars, drones and helicopters.
m.conflict-pve.intro.1: Built on Gramps303's ConflictPVERemixedVanilla2.0 and on the WCS, RHS and ACE suites: over 100 Workshop mods, all declared dependencies, nothing repacked. For intermediate to advanced players who enjoy tactical team play. Lone wolves might shed a little tear.
m.conflict-pve.f.0: Enemy headquarters. Hunter groups only come on intelligence: an enemy drone or a patrol that spots you or your vehicle. They head where you should be by now, search the area, march in column and spread into a line on contact.
m.conflict-pve.f.1: Generator capture (with Enhanced Compositions). Repair the FIA HQ generator with a wrench, then fill it with fuel (18 L, about 20 s) while the base siren sounds. Radio contact with your HQ is required.
m.conflict-pve.f.2: Fuel economy. A running generator gives its base 10 supplies per litre, never more than the base storage holds. A friendly fuel depot or the deployable M1091 fuel truck keeps it full.
m.conflict-pve.f.3: Sabotage and breaching. About 30 s after a capture, the nearest enemy soldier tries to disable the generator. Wall it in with HESCO and a breacher blows the closest wall: kill him or defuse the charges within 20 s.
m.conflict-pve.f.4: Hard HESCO. Bullets, grenades and vehicles do nothing. Explosives only: 1, 2 or 4 M112 charges depending on size.
m.conflict-pve.f.5: AI doctrine. Fire discipline, tactical withdrawal, engagement ranges based on posture, movement, weather and night.
m.conflict-pve.f.6: Enemy mortars with forward observers, real ballistics and counter-battery play.
m.conflict-pve.f.7: Overwatch sniper teams: a Spetsnaz sniper with a spotter, or alone.
m.conflict-pve.f.8: Drone warfare. Enemy drones you can hide from (posture, foliage), jammers, drones kept in saved loadouts.
m.conflict-pve.f.9: Hunter squads and helicopter paratroopers sized by the number of nearby players.
m.conflict-pve.f.10: AI rocket launchers also target infantry, in every faction: stay spread out.
m.conflict-pve.f.11: Modern US AI in MultiCam; enemies with matching camouflage and red armbands; Spetsnaz paratroopers in black and A-TACS.
m.conflict-pve.f.12: C-RAM that engages all threats, with an attack siren (Main Base only).
m.conflict-pve.f.13: Ranks saved across server and mission restarts.
m.conflict-pve.f.14: Complete US arsenal, unlocked at every rank, except the Golden Shovel (Sergeant).
m.conflict-pve.f.15: The shovel cuts trees, not just bushes, and stumps are removed.
m.conflict-pve.f.16: Ally markers: icons above allies (50 m, 300 m through optics), squad members in team colour, names up close.
m.conflict-pve.f.17: Consistent garage and helipad costs: a better vehicle never costs less in supplies, XP or rank.
m.conflict-pve.f.18: Patrol trucks run either a supply run or a troop transport.
m.conflict-pve.inc.0: Weather director: drizzle, rain, thunderstorm fronts, dawn mist and fog banks with smooth transitions. Bad weather grounds enemy drones and aircraft.
m.conflict-pve.inc.1: Night gear: some enemy soldiers carry night-vision goggles or thermal scopes, and see accordingly.
m.conflict-pve.inc.2: Attack plans: L-shaped attack, hammer and anvil, mortar first, infiltration, feint, harassment and road ambush, chosen from what the HQ knows.
m.conflict-pve.inc.3: Road ambushes: nine kinds, from mines and AT teams to FPV corridors and pre-registered mortar strikes; persistent roadblocks on the roads you use most.
m.conflict-pve.inc.4: Air strikes and Geran raids: guided glide bombs, cruise missiles on captured bases, Su-57 reconnaissance passes, Geran launch trucks you can hunt down.
m.conflict-pve.inc.5: Drone teams: the enemy Mavic no longer drops grenades; it circles above its target, guides strikes, and a light under it shows its state.
m.conflict-pve.inc.6: Radio alerts: short radio hints when a drone watches you, a group comes for you, or a strike is on its way.
m.conflict-pve.inc.7: FIA and regular USSR soldiers in Czech Vz95 uniforms.
m.conflict-pve.admin.0: Our systems are set from $profile:INDFORGE_*/config.json files: AI doctrine, enemy HQ, mortars, generator capture, hunter size, drone sight, name tags, patrol trucks, shovel, session report, and more. The admin console lists every key with its help text.
m.conflict-pve.admin.1: Third-party systems keep their own files: $profile:CET/CETConfig.json (hunters), $profile:MBS_AutoHeliSpawner/config.json (helicopters), $profile:EnhancedCompositions/Garrison.json (garrisons, to switch on).
m.conflict-pve.admin.2: The server runs the version published on the Workshop: an update arrives only after it is republished.

m.forest.tag: Conflict PvE in the dense forests of Belleau Wood.
m.forest.intro.0: INDFORGE - Forest brings the INDFORGE - Conflict PvE experience to the Belleau Wood map: the same AI, doctrine, arsenal, ranks and settings as on Everon, with its own bases, relay stations, roadblocks, patrols and vehicle spawn points.
m.forest.intro.1: It requires INDFORGE - Conflict PvE. A change made in Conflict PvE reaches Forest once Conflict PvE is republished on the Workshop.
m.forest.f.0: Conflict bases, relay stations and starting points adapted to Belleau Wood.
m.forest.f.1: 15 forest roadblock setups with their guards.
m.forest.f.2: Every capturable base defended by 3 to 4 groups: rifle squad, machine-gun team, fire team, AT team.
m.forest.f.3: Spetsnaz Overwatch snipers, teams and lone snipers, tracking prey in open fields around the bases.
m.forest.f.4: Foot patrols between bases, armed and transport vehicle patrols, civilian presence.
m.forest.f.5: AI spawn points named after what they really spawn, for easier admin and editing.
m.forest.f.6: Random weapon caches: switched off on this map for now, coming soon.
m.forest.admin.0: Same server profile files as Conflict PvE: the settings and commands of the admin console apply here too.
m.forest.admin.1: Set game.scenarioId to the scenario ID above and use the full mods block below: Forest, Conflict PvE and its dependencies, Belleau Wood and the two railway mods.
m.forest.credits: Belleau Wood map by Thinwheat01. RailwayGenerator and RailEnfusionRedux by TilW. And every creator of the Conflict PvE dependencies.
m.ai-framework.tag: Modular, map-agnostic AI for PvE scenarios: helicopter patrols, garrisons, ground patrols.
m.ai-framework.intro.0: INDFORGE - AI Framework adds configurable hostile helicopter patrols, military garrisons and ground patrols to compatible Conflict scenarios.
m.ai-framework.intro.1: Everything is set from a JSON file in the server profile, without touching the code. Map support depends on the points of interest the scenario exposes.
m.ai-framework.f.0: Combat Heli Spawner. A hostile USSR patrol helicopter appears near the biggest group of players, anchored on a point of interest (military base, airport, city, village…), with a full crew and a configurable AI skill, from Noob to Expert.
m.ai-framework.f.1: Scripted flight controller, not the engine's AI flight: patrol loop over nearby points of interest, altitude hold, banked turns.
m.ai-framework.f.2: Automatic cleanup. Shot down, pilot or rotor lost, landed or in water: the wreck despawns and the slot is released after a cooldown (23 minutes in total with the shipped values).
m.ai-framework.f.3: Military garrisons. Each eligible point of interest gets two patrols, one tight and one wide, and small static teams hold towers, bunkers and watchtowers.
m.ai-framework.f.4: Priority under the AI cap. The engine keeps about 128 AI active at once: helicopter crew first, then close patrols and building posts, then wide patrols.
m.ai-framework.setup.0: Subscribe to the mod and add it to your server's mods.
m.ai-framework.setup.1: In the World Editor, add the INDFORGE components to the GameModeCampaign (or base GameMode) entity of your mission.
m.ai-framework.setup.2: Copy the shipped ServerProfile/INDF_CombatHeliSpawner/config.json to $profile:INDF_CombatHeliSpawner/config.json. That copy is the one read, once, at startup.
m.ai-framework.setup.3: Per world: on the FIA CampaignFactionManager, add USSR to Friendly Factions Ids, and FIA on the USSR one. Without it the two factions fight each other.
m.ai-framework.setup.4: Restart the server after every change. In Workbench, close and reopen it: it caches the file.
m.ai-framework.admin.0: Do not raise MaxActiveHelicopters: the flight is scripted and has no collision avoidance between aircraft.
m.ai-framework.admin.1: At startup the log must show [INDF_CombatHeliConfig] LoadFromFile SUCCESS, then the POI scan and the garrison population.
m.ai-framework.admin.2: No helicopter? Check the player count (MinimumPlayersToActivate) and the 23-minute wait after a kill.
m.enhanced-compositions.tag: Compact Conflict compositions, generator capture and AI garrisons.
m.enhanced-compositions.intro.0: Enhanced Compositions gives mission makers, Game Masters and players simpler Conflict compositions, easy to adapt to missions or maps where the Conflict mod is hard to set up, plus a new way to capture bases and AI garrisons that protect buildings.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.0: Compositions: small antenna, ammo storage (WIP), field hospital (WIP), vehicle maintenance and living area for US and USSR, the living area with the full list of AI groups in its menu; small FIA headquarters, tent and hut, each with or without a generator.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.1: FIA HQ generator. Starts out of order and dry, cannot be destroyed. Repair it with a wrench (8 s, any faction), fill it with a jerry can: it runs until the tank is empty. A crate in each generator HQ holds a wrench and a jerry can.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.2: Commander actions grouped on the HQ table, next to the construction panel: logistics, combat support and construction.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.3: Garrisons. Barracks: 5 soldiers patrolling plus the full unit list. Armory, vehicle workshops and fuel depot: a two-person team. Antenna: a two-person recon team.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.4: Garrison rules. The first group is free. A wiped group returns after 10 minutes if supplies allow and no enemy is near. Not recruitable, not saved. Corporals and above switch it with the Garrison action.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.5: Vehicle service while a guard lives: the fuel depot refuels allied vehicles for free; the workshops repair and rearm them for supplies.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.6: Golden Shovel in the US and USSR arsenals, from the rank of Sergeant.
m.enhanced-compositions.f.7: With INDFORGE - Conflict PvE only: capture by fuel, supplies from the generator and enemy sabotage.
m.enhanced-compositions.admin.1: The file is created on first launch with "Enabled": false: set it to true to turn garrisons on. The mod never overwrites it.
m.auc-factions.tag: Ukrainian, Russian and assault-battalion factions for the Arma Ukraine Community.
m.auc-factions.intro.0: AUC - Factions is a specific configuration of the WCS NATO and RU factions, and a little more, for the PvPvE servers of the [AUC] Arma Ukraine Community. It builds on these mods for stability and immersive gameplay.
m.auc-factions.f.0: BLUFOR: you play as the Ukrainian armed forces.
m.auc-factions.f.1: OPFOR: you play as the 214th Independent Assault Battalion, the only battalion authorised to play as enemy forces.
m.auc-factions.f.2: INDFOR: you fight the Russian armed forces.
m.auc-factions.f.3: Brings in, as dependencies, Realistic Combat Drones - WCS and kuka's Vampire UAV and FPV drones.
m.auc-factions.credits: Thanks to the WCS and RHS teams, SalamiBoiDev, FriendlyModder and kuka-.
m.auc-vehicles.tag: The vehicle pool of the Arma Ukraine Community servers.
m.auc-vehicles.intro.0: AUC - Vehicles is a specific configuration of several vehicle mods, with a few additional changes, built for the [AUC] Arma Ukraine Community.
m.auc-vehicles.credits: Thanks to the WCS, RHS, CIE and FRM teams and to every vehicle creator in the dependencies.
m.auc-conflict.tag: PvPvE Conflict for the Arma Ukraine Community, starting on Kolguyev.
m.auc-conflict.intro.0: AUC - Conflict is a specific configuration of the Conflict mode for the [AUC] Arma Ukraine Community. It relies on WCS_Core for stability and suits several kinds of terrain.
m.cherchetoi-rp-clothing.tag: Role-play clothing for the CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE community.
m.cherchetoi-rp-clothing.intro.0: ChercheToi RP - Clothing is a specific configuration of several clothing mods, with a few changes, for the CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE role-play community.
m.cherchetoi-rp-clothing.f.0: Civilian, biker and press outfits gathered from the clothing mods in the dependencies.
m.cherchetoi-rp-clothing.f.1: SAMU emergency-medical equipment, by CTRP team contributor Captain Valaaks.
m.cherchetoi-rp-props.tag: Role-play props for the CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE community.
m.cherchetoi-rp-props.intro.0: ChercheToi RP - Props is a specific configuration of props for the CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE community, built on Lakes Dan's work for the Faircroft Islands.
m.cherchetoi-rp-props.f.0: Props from Faircroft Islands and Brit Props by Lakes Dan.
m.cherchetoi-rp-props.f.1: Palm trees from Palmtree by Ben.obj.
m.cherchetoi-rp-vehicles.tag: The role-play vehicle pool of the CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE community.
m.cherchetoi-rp-vehicles.intro.0: ChercheToi RP - Vehicles is a specific configuration of 32 vehicle and equipment mods, with a few changes, for the CHERCHE TOI – RP LIFE role-play community.
m.cherchetoi-rp-vehicles.f.0: Cars, SUVs, vans, a bus, pickups, motorbikes, bicycles, karts and boats from the community's favourite vehicle mods.
m.cherchetoi-rp-vehicles.f.1: Trucks such as the KamAZ 5350, and the SA342 Gazelle helicopter.
m.lav-25-desert.tag: The LAV-25 Piranha in Operation Desert Storm colours.
m.lav-25-desert.intro.0: The LAV-25 Piranha is a light armoured vehicle developed in 1981–1982 by General Motors Canada. It entered service with the United States Marine Corps in 1983, with 758 units delivered.
m.lav-25-desert.intro.1: Armed with an M242 Bushmaster 25 mm cannon and a coaxial M240 machine gun, it comes here in the four colours used during Operation Desert Storm, on 17 January 1991. A thought for the veterans of that war.
m.lav-25-desert.f.0: LAV-25 (MC) in four Desert Storm colour schemes.
m.lav-25-desert.f.1: M242 Bushmaster 25 mm cannon and coaxial M240.
m.modern-fia.tag: A modernised FIA: bullpup rifle, ballistic helmets, body armour.
m.modern-fia.intro.0: As part of a programme to modernise its infantry, the Freedom and Independence Army (FIA) receives new equipment.
m.modern-fia.f.0: Promet bullpup assault rifle in 6.5×39 mm, 30-round magazine.
m.rcd-rhs.tag: SalamiBoiDev's drones and jammer backpack in every RHS arsenal.
m.rcd-rhs.intro.0: Realistic Combat Drones - RHS adds the full set of SalamiBoiDev's drone equipment to the RHS arsenals.
m.rcd-rhs.f.0: FPV drones, dropper drones and recon drones, each with its battery.
m.rcd-rhs.f.3: In the FFA, ION, RHS MSV and USMC arsenals.
m.rcd-wcs.tag: SalamiBoiDev's drones in the WCS arsenals, and a buildable TPN-19 jammer.
m.rcd-wcs.intro.0: Realistic Combat Drones - WCS adds the full set of SalamiBoiDev's drone equipment to the WCS arsenals of the US (BLUFOR) and the USSR (OPFOR), with costs and ranks, plus a drone jammer you can build in Conflict bases.
m.rcd-wcs.f.0: FPV-RPG drone (125), FPV drone (100), dropper drone (75), recon drone (50), batteries (2), controller and goggles (0): Corporal.
m.rcd-wcs.f.1: Jammer bag (100): Private. Long-range drone antenna (200): Sergeant. Drone command station (300): Lieutenant.
m.rcd-wcs.f.2: TPN-19 radar jammer, buildable in Conflict bases by US, USSR or FIA (cost 300): jams drones within 250 m as soon as it is built. ON/OFF switch on the side door handle, usable by anyone. Generator sounds follow its state. Also available to Game Masters.
m.rcd-wcs.f.3: Friend or foe: a jammer worn, carried or built into a base no longer cuts the drones of its own side and allies. A jammer left on the ground jams everyone.
m.rcd-wcs.f.4: Drone controller in the secondary weapon slot; a mask can be worn with drone goggles.
m.solo-push-pull.tag: Push or pull any car or truck on your own. Even the BTR.
m.solo-push-pull.intro.0: A simple change to the vanilla unflip action that came with Arma Reforger 1.2.0.92: now, even alone, you can push or pull any car or truck, and even the BTR, like a real superhero.
m.solo-push-pull.intro.1: Compatible with all mods. Caution: an overdose of Push-Pull may cause health problems.
m.solo-push-pull.f.0: Solo push and pull on cars, trucks and armoured vehicles.
m.solo-push-pull.f.1: No dependency, compatible with all mods.
m.solo-push-pull.credits: A big thank you to the Conflict In Europe team [CIE] for putting this mod in the spotlight.
m.talibanmod-red-side-v2.tag: FIA and USSR turned into insurgents of the Arab world, for Task Force Baguette.
m.talibanmod-red-side-v2.intro.0: TalibanMod Red Side V2, made for Task Force Baguette, turns the FIA and the USSR into OPFOR fighters from various rebellions of the Arab world. PvE Conflict available.
m.talibanmod-red-side-v2.f.3: Arabic inscriptions on FIA and USSR signs.
m.talibanmod-red-side-v2.credits: Thanks to V-lst for Insurgents SAF and to zelik for Zeliks Character.
m.off-road-vehicles.tag: Off-road 4×4 and 6×6 vehicles for limitless exploration.
m.off-road-vehicles.intro.0: Off-Road Vehicles brings several 4×4 and 6×6 vehicles to discover Everon like never before, with a Game Master scenario to try them.
m.off-road-vehicles.intro.1: On standby: the mod may be merged with UAZ-452 Offroad.
m.off-road-vehicles.f.0: 4×4 and 6×6 vehicles in six colours: blue, grey, orange, savanna, snow, suburban.
m.off-road-vehicles.f.1: A repair and medical assistance version.
m.off-road-vehicles.f.3: Tip: if forward gear is not enough, reverse has more torque.
m.uaz-452-offroad.tag: The UAZ-452 "Bukhanka", reworked for the mountains.
m.uaz-452-offroad.intro.0: The UAZ-452 Classic is an off-road van built at the Ulyanovsk plant since 1965. We reworked its design to make a real Bukhanka ready to take on the mountains: 110 hp and more to take you beyond the horizon.
m.uaz-452-offroad.intro.1: On standby: the mod may be merged with Off-Road Vehicles.
m.uaz-452-offroad.f.0: Civilian 4×4 in eight colours: khaki, red, yellow, green, blue, dark blue, purple, pink.
m.uaz-452-offroad.f.1: Repair version for the Civilian, FIA and USSR factions.
deps.unreleased: The dependency list will be published with the mod.
intel.lvl_rng: Opens fire on infantry within (standing / crouched / prone)
ui.see_cfg: Every setting of this mod in the admin console
ui.cfg_cpve: Values from the INDFORGE - Conflict PvE reference profile.

about.giants: We move forward “on the shoulders of giants”: our creations build on the work of other creators and depend on it; nothing is repacked. But we don't stop there: some of our work is strong enough to stand on its own, without depending on anything else… Either way, pooling our efforts is and will remain an exceptional and deeply rewarding adventure for our team.
